title: Sharper than a sword (Hebrews 4:12)
hookLine: the word of God is living and effectual

lines: ONLY GOD KNOWS WHO WROTE IT DOWN.
cards: The letter to the Hebrews names no author. The Douay-Rheims heads it as Paul's, and the Church long counted it among his letters, but early Christians also suggested Barnabas, or Luke, or Clement of Rome.
Origen, the scholar of Alexandria, said, more or less, that only God knows who wrote it down. It reads less like a letter than a sermon, for Christians who were tired and tempted to drift away.
Hebrews and James start today, and this preacher has a lot to say about how God speaks.

teach.h: TODAY, IF YOU HEAR HIS VOICE.
teach.b: He's just been quoting a psalm: today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts. Today. The psalm was centuries old, and he treats it as spoken right now, to his listeners.

Then today's verse: "For the word of God is living and effectual, and more piercing than any two edged sword; and reaching unto the division of the soul and the spirit, of the joints also and the marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart."
Living: not a fossil. Effectual is the Greek energes: active, at work. It does things.
Then the sword. Look at what it cuts: soul from spirit, joints from marrow.

teach.h: A SCALPEL MORE THAN A WEAPON.
teach.b: Some readers hear surgery here more than battle, a scalpel more than a weapon, reaching places you can't reach yourself and showing what's actually there. Discerner, in Greek, is kritikos: one able to judge.

teach.h: IT READS YOU WHILE YOU READ IT.
teach.b: In Hebrews' picture, the word of God reads you while you read it. The next verse says it plainly: nothing is hidden from his sight, everything is naked and open to his eyes. That could sound frightening.
Read another way, it's the start of healing: you can't treat what you can't see.

teach.h: THE WORD OF GOD IS LIVING AND EFFECTUAL.
teach.b: Catholics honor the word with their bodies. At Mass the Book of the Gospels can be carried in procession, held high, incensed and kissed.
The Second Vatican Council said the Church has always venerated the Scriptures just as it venerates the Lord's body, and that in them the Father meets his children and speaks with them.

how: At Mass the Book of the Gospels may be carried in the entrance procession, placed on the altar, incensed and kissed before the Gospel is proclaimed; Catholics stand to hear the Gospel.

o: one able to judge, a discerner
a critic who finds fault with others
a sharp sword with two edges

games.q: inside the verse — tap the pairs.
p: a surgeon's cut, not a battle
said only God knows the author

s: Hebrews names Paul as its author
the text names no author; the Church long counted it among Paul's letters, and early Christians suggested others too.
Origen said only God knows who wrote Hebrews
more or less: who wrote it down, he said, God knows.
the sword image is about attacking unbelievers
it cuts soul from spirit, joints from marrow: it reaches inside the hearer.

games.q: you're the preacher of Hebrews, quoting an old psalm, 'today if you shall hear his voice'. how do you treat it?
o: as history: words for people long ago.
as spoken today, to your listeners now.
games.why: he treats it as living now: "the word of God is living and effectual."

practice: Take a verse that has ever unsettled you, or today's: the word of God is living and effectual. Say it slowly, once, without arguing or defending yourself, and notice where it lands: a worry, a habit, an old wound.
If you pray, ask God to show you what's there and to heal it; if not, simply notice what the words uncovered, without judging it.

wordCard.voice: Kritikos, one able to judge. Hebrews' picture of God's word: living, at work, discerning the thoughts and intents of the heart. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: living and effectual. Not a fossil, but at work. Six hundred days now.
